approachQuestion.prompt:
Longest Segment with at Most Two Symbols

The array `events` contains lowercase English letters in their original order. Return the length of the longest contiguous segment containing at most two distinct letters. A segment of length 0 is allowed. Use it only if no non-empty valid segment exists.

Limits and assumptions:
• 0 ≤ n ≤ 200000; each value is one lowercase letter from a to z.
• A segment must be contiguous; leave the input unchanged.
• There are only 26 possible letters; return a length.

Examples:
1. events = ["a","b","a","c","c","c","b","d"] → 4, for example ["a","c","c","c"], which contains two distinct letters.
2. events = ["x","y","z"] → 2.
3. events = [] → 0.

Choose one approach.
constraints: 0 ≤ n ≤ 200000; each value is one lowercase letter from a to z.
A segment must be contiguous; leave the input unchanged.
There are only 26 possible letters; the result is a length.

options.text: Extend the right boundary while tracking the count of each letter in the window and the number of letters with a positive count. If there are more than two, move the left boundary until the condition holds again. Update the best length after each step.
options.feedback: Letter counts show exactly when a letter has left the window, so the boundaries can move without losing valid candidates.

options.text: After each new letter, scan the whole current segment to count its distinct letters. If there are three, move the left boundary and recount until at most two remain.
options.feedback: Recounting gives the correct condition for every input, but reads many of the same positions again instead of updating counts as the boundary moves.

options.text: Keep only a set of letters in the window. When the left boundary moves, remove the outgoing letter from the set without checking whether it still occurs in the window.
options.feedback: A set does not store occurrence counts. In ["a","b","a","c"], removing the first a does not remove the other a; losing that fact can make the method accept three distinct letters as two.

options.text: Consider only segments of length two and return the greatest valid length among them.
options.feedback: A valid segment can be longer than two. For ["x","x","x","x"], the answer is 4, not 2.

feedback.reason: Check whether the window state records enough information to know when each letter has left the segment.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the method “Track counts for the 26 letters while moving the left boundary,” choose one pair: running time and additional space.
constraints: Analyze only the named method. Do not count the input or returned value as additional space.
There is no recursion or call stack.

options.text: O(n log n) time, O(1) additional space

feedback.reason: Each position enters the window once and leaves it at most once. The frequency array has a fixed size of 26, regardless of the input length.

details.correctness: After each extension, move the left boundary until the window contains at most two distinct letters. A count reaching zero tells us exactly that a letter is no longer present. Both boundaries move only forward, and each position causes a constant number of updates.
details.alternatives: Rescanning the entire window is correct but may read the same positions many times as the window grows. A set without counts cannot tell whether another copy of a removed letter remains. A fixed window of length two misses longer valid segments.

methodReveal.title: Letter counts inside the window
methodReveal.description: Keep a count for each of the 26 letters and track how many counts are positive. Add the letter on the right. If more than two counts are positive, remove letters from the left and update their counts until the condition holds again.
